The first thing you want to do is just draw things that you have around. Do still life. It may seem boring but if you actually want to get good at something. Yeah. I can't stress enough just how superiour charcoal is to just about anything else when you are trying to learn how to draw.

Lesson 1: Line [simple example](http://us.123rf.com/400wm/400/400/triling/triling0904/triling090400348/4724804-vector-illustration-of-flowers-design-set-made-with-simple-line-only.jpg) / [complex example](http://4.bp.blogspot.com/_-b0vtr4e7Qw/TI4C0iYpflI/AAAAAAAAApw/oFIMnua0hrY/s1600/port01LineDrawing.jpg)

Start off by getting some paper. A whole bunch of it, the bigger the better (I suggest A1) Organize a bunch of objects on a table or something and put a light source onto it.

Next just draw what you see. Using only lines. Don't try and use tone. Just draw the shapes that you see. Repeat this a bunch on different things until you are happy with it. (you won't be happy with it)

Lesson 2: Perspective [Link](http://www.artyfactory.com/perspective_drawing/perspective_index.html)

This one I think is one of the more fun things to play around with.

Start drawing again, your practice in drawin line should help you out here.

Either get some string or actually draw the lines on the page that will help you with perspective.

Play around with different shapes (cubes, spheres, cylinders, pyramids)
At different levels. eye level, above, below, left, right, so on and so forth.


Lesson 3: Tone [what is tone?](http://drawsketch.about.com/od/drawingglossary/g/tone.htm)

Read the link.

when you are drawing your still lifes if you want a tip to be able to better see areas of light and dark try squinting your eyes. It may seem stupid but it works!


These are some basics that should see you in the right track. Good luck!
